docs.title: Network Observability Runbook
docs.text: Welcome to the internal documentation for the Network Observability and Alerting stack.

docs.title: Project Purpose
docs.text: Transforming a rooted Android device (Snapdragon 888) into a low-power, dedicated network observability appliance via an Ubuntu chroot environment.

docs.title: High-Level Topology
docs.text: Android Kernel -> Ubuntu Chroot -> Supervisor Daemon -> Telemetry Stack (Prometheus, Loki, Grafana, Promtail, Blackbox Exporter, Alertmanager) -> Mesh Network (Tailscale) -> Slack Notifications.

docs.title: System Resource Footprint
docs.text:
• Memory Management: Low memory profile by running native Linux binaries directly.
  • CPU Efficiency: Leveraging the Snapdragon 888 ARM64 architecture natively.
  • Optimization: Disabling unnecessary background LLM daemons to preserve resources.

docs.title: 1. Environment Setup
docs.text:
• Hardware: Realme GT2 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 1).
  • OS: PixelOS, rooted via Magisk.
  • Chroot: Ubuntu 24.04 native environment sharing the Android kernel.

docs.title: 2. Process Management
docs.text: Because systemd is incompatible with the shared Android kernel, supervisor is used to manage all background daemons. * Install: apt-get install supervisor * Config Location: /etc/supervisor/conf.d/

docs.title: 3. Tailscale Failover (Multi-WAN)
docs.text: The device utilizes a custom Magisk script (tailscale_failover.sh) to actively manage routing tables and prevent Android "ghost tables" from interfering with Tailscale's mesh networking when switching between Cellular and Wi-Fi interfaces.

docs.title: 1. Pipeline Architecture
docs.text: External Device (UDP/514) -> rsyslog (Relay) -> promtail (RFC5424/TCP/1514) -> loki (Storage).

docs.title: 2. Configuration Details
docs.text:
• Loki: Configured for 7-day retention to prevent excessive UFS flash storage degradation.
  • rsyslog: Acts as a lightweight relay listening on standard port UDP/514, forwarding cleanly formatted logs to Promtail via TCP.
  • Promtail: Scrapes local logs and receives forwarded syslog data, pushing it to Loki on http://127.0.0.1:3100.

docs.title: SOP-003: Gemini AI Middleware & UI Deployment
1. Overview
docs.text: A custom FastAPI Python application that queries Loki logs via LogQL, streams context to the Gemini API (gemini-3.6-flash), and serves a Tailwind CSS web UI.

docs.title: 2. Deployment
docs.text:
• Location: /opt/gemini-noc/
  • Dependencies: fastapi, uvicorn, google-generativeai, requests.
  • Execution: Managed by Supervisor. Listens on http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: 3. UI Features
docs.text: The integrated frontend (/static/index.html) provides natural language querying, time range selection (15m, 1h, 6h, 24h), severity filtering, and raw log evidence extraction.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: An autonomous Python script (proactive_alert.py) that periodically scans the network logs for critical anomalies and hardware failures.

docs.title: 2. Execution Flow
docs.text:
• Schedule: Runs every 15 minutes via the local cron daemon.
  • Query: Fetches all logs marked with severity=error from Loki for the past 15 minutes.
  • Analysis: The logs are fed to the gemini-3.6-flash model with instructions to identify critical anomalies or repeating hardware noise.
  • Alerting: If the AI determines an anomaly exists, it prefixes the output with STATUS: ALERT and pushes a notification directly to a configured Slack Webhook URL.

docs.title: 1. Host & Containerization Layer
docs.text:
• Chroot Isolation: Runs natively on top of the Android Linux kernel at /data/local/tmp/ubuntu.
  • Supervisor: A process controller managing all service lifecycles (/etc/supervisor/conf.d/observability.conf).

docs.title: 2. Log Ingestion Flow
docs.text: rsyslog receiving network syslogs -> Promtail parsing and shipping -> Loki indexing (http://127.0.0.1:3100).

docs.title: 3. Metrics & Probing Flow
docs.text: Blackbox Exporter performing ICMP probes every 5s -> Prometheus scraping /probe endpoints (http://127.0.0.1:9090).

docs.title: 4. Alerting Pipeline
docs.text: Prometheus evaluating rules (/opt/prometheus/alerts/icmp.yml) -> Alertmanager (http://127.0.0.1:9093) -> Incoming Slack Webhook (#general).

docs.title: 5. Visualization Layer
docs.text: Grafana (http://127.0.0.1:3000) querying Loki and Prometheus data sources.

docs.title: CLI & API Reference Manual
docs.text: A cheat sheet for all system interfaces.

docs.title: 1. CLI Commands
docs.text:
• promtool: Validation commands for rules and main config.
  • logger: Generating synthetic test logs (logger -p daemon.err "test message").
  • supervisorctl: Process control commands.

docs.title: 2. LogQL Reference
docs.text:
• Basic query: {job="syslog"}
  • Filter query: {job="syslog"} |= "error" != "keepalive"
  • Aggregation query: sum(count_over_time({job="syslog"} |= "block" [1h]))

docs.title: 3. API Endpoints
docs.text:
• Prometheus Metrics: GET http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics
  • Loki Query Range: GET http://127.0.0.1:3100/loki/api/v1/query_range
  • Alertmanager API: POST http://127.0.0.1:9093/api/v2/alerts
  • Blackbox Probe: GET http://127.0.0.1:9115/probe?module=icmp&target=8.8.8.8

docs.title: Troubleshooting & Diagnostic Guide
docs.text: Diagnostic workflows for common infrastructure failures in the observability stack.

docs.title: 1. Prometheus "Spawn Error" or Startup Crash
docs.text:
• Cause: Invalid YAML indentation or duplicate root keys (alerting:, rule_files:) caused by append commands (cat >>).
  • Fix: Inspecting /var/log/supervisor/prometheus-stderr*.log and running promtool check config.

docs.title: 2. Blackbox Exporter Permission Denied (ICMP)
docs.text:
• Cause: Lack of cap_net_raw socket capabilities inside the chroot environment.
  • Fix: Executing setcap cap_net_raw+ep /opt/blackbox_exporter/blackbox_exporter.

docs.title: 3. Alertmanager Webhook Failures
docs.text:
• Cause: Misconfigured Slack Webhook URL, wrong channel name, or network unreachability.
  • Fix: Testing Slack connection using direct curl payloads to http://127.0.0.1:9093/api/v2/alerts.

docs.title: 4. Loki Log Ingestion Gaps
docs.text:
• Cause: Time drift between Android host and Ubuntu chroot, or Promtail offset errors.
  • Fix: Ensure NTP synchronization and check Promtail logs for position file errors.

docs.title: 1. Chroot Environment Deployment
docs.text:
• Require Root privileges (su) on Android.
  • Mount essential pseudo-filesystems (proc, sys, dev, pts).
  • Enter the chroot shell.

docs.title: 2. Base Packages Installation
docs.text: Ensure the following packages are installed: supervisor, rsyslog, curl, python3, libcap2-bin.

docs.title: 3. Observability Stack Binary Installation Paths
docs.text:
• /opt/prometheus/
  • /opt/loki/
  • /opt/promtail/
  • /opt/grafana/
  • /opt/blackbox_exporter/
  • /opt/alertmanager/

docs.title: 4. Supervisor Master Configuration
docs.text: The Supervisor master configuration is located at /etc/supervisor/conf.d/observability.conf, which manages all binaries simultaneously.

docs.title: Standard Operating Procedure: Add or Remove Target IPs
docs.text: This document details how to modify the list of network hosts monitored by Blackbox Exporter and Prometheus.

docs.title: Step 1: Modify Prometheus Configuration
docs.text:
Open /opt/prometheus/prometheus.yml in an editor:

sudo nano /opt/prometheus/prometheus.yml

Locate the blackbox_icmp job under scrape_configs:

- job_name: 'blackbox_icmp'
    metrics_path: /probe
    params:
      module: [icmp]
    static_configs:
      - targets:
          - 8.8.8.8          # Public DNS / WAN Check
          - 192.168.100.1    # Default Gateway
          - 192.168.102.110  # Local Host
          # Add new IP addresses below

docs.title: Step 2: Restart Prometheus
docs.text:
After modifying and saving the file, restart Prometheus via Supervisor:

supervisorctl restart prometheus

docs.title: Standard Operating Procedure: Managing Probed Targets
docs.text: This document outlines how to add or remove monitored network hosts.

docs.title: Step 1: Edit Target Definitions
docs.text: Edit the target definitions in /opt/prometheus/prometheus.yml. Add or remove IPs under the blackbox_icmp job static_configs.

docs.title: Step 2: Validate YAML Syntax
docs.text:
Validate the YAML syntax using the Promtool validator:

/opt/prometheus/promtool check config /opt/prometheus/prometheus.yml

docs.title: Step 3: Grant Raw Network Permissions
docs.text:
If ICMP probes fail with permission errors, ensure raw network capabilities are granted to Blackbox Exporter:

setcap cap_net_raw+ep /opt/blackbox_exporter/blackbox_exporter

docs.title: Step 4: Reload Prometheus
docs.text:
Apply the changes by restarting Prometheus via Supervisor:

supervisorctl restart prometheus

docs.title: Standard Operating Procedure: Managing Background Services
docs.text: This operational guide details how to manage background daemons using Supervisor.

docs.title: 1. Checking Status
docs.text:
To view the status of all managed services:

supervisorctl status

docs.title: 2. Restarting Individual Services
docs.text:
To restart a specific service, use:

supervisorctl restart <service_name>

docs.title: 3. Reading Live Logs
docs.text:
To follow the live standard output logs for a service:

tail -f /var/log/supervisor/<service_name>*.log

docs.title: 4. Updating Service Definitions
docs.text:
If you edit the master configuration at /etc/supervisor/conf.d/observability.conf, you must reload Supervisor:

supervisorctl reread && supervisorctl update
